parsed.explanation: A trans visitor here faces two stacked state-facing exposures. Nationally, passport markers are restricted to birth sex, 'X' issuance has ended, documents have been confiscated or blocked, and officers are instructed to refuse where sex is doubted and to consider a permanent fraud ineligibility finding. In this division, a law effective 1 July 2026 makes it a misdemeanour (up to a year) for a trans person to use a restroom not matching birth sex — in government buildings and public-facing private businesses, including restaurants, hospitals and gas stations. That is a universal-exposure measure reaching every outing to a café or clinic, with no demonstrated remedy: the challenge filed 30 April 2026 is unresolved and no enforcement record is documented. Custody harm (federal prison and immigration detention) compounds severity. Below the 0.25–0.35 anchors, above the 0.05 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal rules bar self-selected markers and X issuance; reported confiscation/blocked processing and stranding; officers tag refusals and weigh permanent fraud ineligibility where sex is doubted.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-existing X passports remain valid until expiry; litigation by civil-liberties plaintiffs pending; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Division keeps X on its own licences while federal passports carry birth sex — a mismatch a border officer can escalate.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style inmate policies (hair, hormones, psychiatric substitution).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can lead to detention and birth-sex placement, moving the visitor from administrative to custodial exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law effective 1 July 2026 criminalises restroom/changing use by birth sex in government buildings and public-facing private businesses; first offence misdemeanour to one year. Four divisions criminalise such use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: General statute requires willful entry plus refusal to depart and lists exemptions; suit filed 30 April 2026; a 16 June 2026 narrowing of unestablished status.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Reaches every restaurant, fuel stop and hospital visit; no documented working remedy at present.

care_services.exposure: March 2026 law obliges medical professionals, schools and childcare to disclose a trans minor's status to parents within three days; hospitals are covered premises under the facilities law.
care_services.protection: September 2024 ruling letting prisoners receive hormones (resident-facing); no visitor-facing care protection documented.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or routine care for a trans minor or adult risks both disclosure obligations and facility-use liability.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2026 federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups described as 'radically pro-transgender'; justice-department reward memo cites 'radical gender ideology'; a trans student was handcuffed and charged with trespass in a capitol restroom.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal gender-identity hate-crime statute; statement that counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Frames trans advocacy as security matter while local police enforce facility statutes against individuals.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor shares the criminal restroom exposure; disclosure duties to parents within three days; schools barred from non-birth-certificate pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Facilities statute exempts accompanying/chaperoning a child under 12; parental consent routes for resident minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor cannot rely on chaperone exemptions for the minor's own facility use.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific data showing trans violence materially above the general homicide rate; national bias-crime reporting exists.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 divisions cover it in bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence axis is undocumented rather than assessed; recourse is theoretical and uneven by division.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether the June 2026 narrowing survives and the fate of the facilities challenge are unresolved; no enforcement record against visitors identified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil-liberties litigation with six plaintiffs filed before the effect date; legal-aid and advocacy guidance available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Until a court acts, the criminal facilities rule is presumptively operative for the traveller.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor pairs barred detention with invasive administrative review and denial of entry. Here the border friction is comparable or worse (confiscation, lifetime-ineligibility risk), and the division adds a criminal facilities statute reaching private businesses — a traveller-facing sanction, not mere paperwork. Rates below.

There a hospitality code worked through escalation, producing a room and an ombudsman contact. Here no working protection is documented for facilities at all; the operative rule is criminal, litigation is unresolved, and federal entry rules add exposure. Substantially below.

That anchor involves coerced extortionate detention cycles and threats of prison with no formal protection. This jurisdiction likewise lacks functioning protection, but adds a statutory universal exposure plus documented federal custody harm; comparable severity, broader reach. Rated marginally below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a federal document gate plus a division criminal-facilities regime. Federally, the traveller's marker comes from a passport system that no longer accommodates X markers, with reported confiscation, refusal instructions where sex is doubted, and a discretionary lifetime fraud finding. Locally, the effective 1 July 2026 law makes every ordinary restroom use in a restaurant, hospital or venue a potential misdemeanour carrying up to a year, with an unresolved challenge and no working remedy documented. Custody, if entered, is documented as abusive. No anti-trans violence rate above background is documented, and national hate-crime coverage exists but is unevenly implemented — protection is theoretical while the exposures are operative.
